The diagram above shows the angle $\theta ={200}^{∘}$ in the coordinate plane.  What is its reference angle ${\theta }_{R}?$

${\theta }_{R}=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/7e7ddf9e0a6edbfd5521ca5de1d718ab9c66b7e0a96ed8d52798fd16daf63aa5.png)

The reference angle, denoted ${\theta }_{R},$  is the angle that $\theta ={200}^{∘}$ makes with the $x$-axis.

As $\theta $ is in the third quadrant, its reference angle is given by

$$
{\theta }_{R}=\theta -{180}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
{\theta }_{R}={200}^{∘}-{180}^{∘}={20}^{∘}.
$$
